note: You edit this file by hand. status can be done, doing or todo. Add a new line to 'log' whenever something important happens (a problem, a fix, a decision). The dashboard reads this file.

log.title: First versions of both Scouts
log.detail: Built the Bitcoin Scout and Gold Scout. Test runs on made-up sample data passed.

log.title: Problem: unrelated stories
log.detail: The bans search returned stories that only matched the word 'lawsuit'. Fix: added a check that the headline is about the asset.

log.title: Problem: trusted list too narrow
log.detail: Too few stories passed. Added BBC, The Guardian, NYT and NBC. Removed CoinDesk, The Block and Kitco because of conflicts of interest.

log.title: First real Gold run
log.detail: Read the Fed calendar (54 meetings) and the BLS calendar (48 releases) from the official websites.

log.title: Problem: no trusted stories for central bank buying and ETF flows
log.detail: Of 57 and 55 stories found, none came from approved websites. Plan: use the SEC for Bitcoin and the World Gold Council monthly data for central banks.

log.title: Problem: old event, new article
log.detail: An article published hours ago can be about an event from days ago, so the 24-hour age check is not enough. Fix planned: the Supervisor will remember events it has already seen.

log.title: Added a summary box
log.detail: Each Scout now ends with a SUMMARY and a BOTTOM LINE.

log.title: Added SEC official feeds
log.detail: The Bitcoin Scout now reads three SEC feeds directly. The World Gold Council's terms do not allow programs to scrape its website, so that file is downloaded by hand.

log.title: Decision: an official source counts on its own
log.detail: A second source is only needed for news websites. An official source (SEC, Fed, World Gold Council) is proof by itself. A social media post can only start a Watch.

log.title: Built the Supervisor
log.detail: Groups stories about the same event (shared names, amounts and key words), applies the proof rules, remembers every event so an old event with a new article is only an update. Wrote 10 tests; all pass.

log.title: Built price tracking
log.detail: Free CoinGecko prices (no key). Gold uses PAX Gold, a token backed by real gold, because CoinGecko has no direct gold price. Records how much the price had already moved when MINT noticed, and the move after 1 hour, 1 day and 7 days.

log.title: Built the Decision agent
log.detail: Uses Claude if an API key is added, otherwise simple rules. It may only use the supplied headlines, must check the event date, and its message is blocked if it sounds like financial advice.

log.title: Problem: running MINT from the terminal is not practical
log.detail: Built the MINT app: double-click an icon, it opens in the browser, runs on a timer and shows what each agent is doing.

log.title: Problem: failed checks looked like 'Calm'
log.detail: When the internet was off, every check failed but the asset still showed Calm. Fix: the state now shows Unknown when all checks fail, and says how many failed.

log.title: First real run of the full system
log.detail: All five agents ran on real data. Real prices from CoinGecko. The Binance hack was reported by 6 organisations and grouped into ONE event.

log.title: Problem: first run alerted on old news
log.detail: With an empty memory, MINT treated everything already in the news as new (for example a follow-up article on the Binance hack). Fix: the first run only learns (no alerts), and follow-up wording like 'after record hack' or 'battles to' now triggers the date check.

log.title: Problem: 6-day-old gold news became an alert
log.detail: Gold searches 7 days back for the weekly summary. Fix: only events first reported in the last 48 hours (gold) or 24 hours (Bitcoin) can become alerts; older gold news goes into the weekly summary.

log.title: Problem: stories filed under the wrong factor
log.detail: Google returned political stories for the 'exchange hacks' search. Fix: each factor has keywords; the headline must contain one, otherwise it is moved to a better factor or dropped as off-topic. Supervisor tests: 15 of 15 pass.

log.title: Research: free ways to read social media
log.detail: X (Twitter) no longer has a free way to read posts (it charges per post read). Free options: Trump's Truth Social posts through the trumpstruth.org public archive feed, public Telegram channels (web preview), Bluesky profile RSS feeds.

log.title: Built the Social Watcher
log.detail: Follows Trump (Truth Social) and Binance announcements (Telegram). A post is kept only if it is under 24 hours old and matches a factor's keywords. A post can only start a Watch, because accounts can be hacked (the SEC's X account was hacked in January 2024).

log.title: Decision: logic first, AI only for reading and writing
log.detail: Proof, age, memory and factor checks stay as fixed rules (easy to test and explain). AI is only used to read the date and write the alert, and is optional: Groq or Gemini (free tiers), Ollama (free, on this computer) or Claude (paid). If the AI fails, the rules take over.

log.title: Problem: page animations kept replaying
log.detail: The page refreshes every few seconds and the fade-in animation played every time. Fix: animations only play when a page is opened.

log.title: Research: best free AI for the Decision agent
log.detail: Groq: free, no card, 1,000 requests a day, does not train on your data - chosen. OpenRouter free models (50 a day) as backup. Gemini free tier may use data to improve Google's products. Note: Grok (xAI) is a different, paid service.

log.title: Built the Telegram bot
log.detail: People sign up with /start and choose Gold, Bitcoin or both. MINT stores only the chat number and the choice. Alerts are sent once, only to the right people, never during test runs, and never if older than 6 hours. 11 tests pass using a pretend Telegram server.

log.title: Added more Telegram message types and a weekly summary
log.detail: People choose 'Alerts only' or 'Everything' (watches, watch updates, heads-ups). Every Sunday MINT sends a summary that checks its own decisions against the price: alerts followed by a clear move, and no-alert decisions with no clear move.

log.title: Decision: smart timing
log.detail: Every 30 minutes normally, every 15 minutes while something is on Watch (to catch the second source faster) or before a scheduled gold event. Never more often than 15 minutes so the free websites are not overloaded.

log.title: Problem: Telegram blocked on our network
log.detail: Connecting the bot and reading the Binance Telegram channel both failed with WinError 10054 (connection cut off). The Telegram app still worked, so the network was blocking Telegram's websites. Fix: added Settings > Check connection, which tests every website MINT uses, and plain-English error messages.

log.title: Every event now has a prediction
log.detail: Each event gets an expected direction from its factor's past pattern, read from the headline (dollar up = gold down, rate cut = gold up, exchange hack = Bitcoin down...). If the headline does not say which way, MINT says 'unclear' instead of guessing. With AI switched on, the Decision agent can give its own prediction for confirmed events.

log.title: Results now judge the prediction, not the price
log.detail: Green means the price moved the way MINT predicted, red the other way. Each event ends as Right, Wrong or No clear move (3% Bitcoin, 1% gold). The History page and weekly summary show prediction accuracy overall, for alerts and per factor.

log.title: Wording: 'Dropped' renamed 'Not confirmed'
log.detail: No event is ever deleted. A Watch that never gets a second source is kept and tracked like every other event; it just does not get an alert.

log.title: Problem: 'certificate verify failed' when connecting to Telegram
log.detail: Python did not trust the certificate it received. Two possible causes: antivirus / a network filter checking secure connections, or the network sending us to a block page. Fix: MINT now checks certificates the same way Windows and the browser do (truststore), and Check connection reads the certificate to say which cause it is. Certificate checks are never switched off, so the bot token stays safe.

log.title: Problem: accuracy looked very low
log.detail: Two problems with how it was measured, not with the agents: (1) events where the price hardly moved counted as failures, and (2) results were judged over 7 days, when other news has mixed in. Fix: judge on the 1-day move (when news moves prices most), count only events where the price clearly moved (1.5% Bitcoin, 0.5% gold), and show 'no clear move' separately. Factor accuracy is only shown with 3 or more results, because 1 or 2 results say nothing.

log.title: Every event gets a prediction
log.detail: When the factor rule cannot read the headline, MINT uses the market's first reaction written in the headline, and if AI is switched on, Groq predicts the rest. Added a Test AI button: the Groq key had never been used because the AI was only called for confirmed events.

log.title: Decision: predict from similar past events, not from the headline
log.detail: Reading the price move from the headline ('gold edges lower') is not a prediction. Now MINT finds the most similar past events (same asset, similar words, same factor, same kind of event) and looks at what the price really did 1 day later, then combines that with the factor pattern. Only events from before the new event are used. Past events come from MINT's own tracking and from real past events I research and add (MINT downloads the real prices). 20 of 20 Supervisor tests pass.

log.title: Problem: Groq AI gave error 1010
log.detail: Groq's website security (Cloudflare) blocks requests that do not say which program they come from. Fix: MINT now sends a User-Agent ('MINT/1.0') with every AI request.

log.title: Decision: report everything
log.detail: Removed the first-run learning (it hid recent events as 'already in the news'). Telegram now sends every event with MINT's view and prediction, every status change and the result 1 day later. A Telegram channel can be used so people only tap Join (Telegram never lets a bot message someone who has not pressed Start).

log.title: Gave the Decision agent knowledge
log.detail: Added factor_knowledge.json (how each factor affects the price, when the effect is bigger or smaller) and a starter library of 36 major past events (FTX, Terra, Bybit, SEC cases, ETF approval, Fed hikes and cuts 2022-2025, inflation and jobs surprises, central bank records, dollar shocks). MINT downloads their real prices. Every event now gets an analysis and a confidence level based on how many similar past events agree. Checking the factor rules against the 36 events found and fixed 4 mistakes.

log.title: Built the cloud version (GitHub Actions)
log.detail: MINT should not depend on my PC being on. GitHub Actions runs all agents every 15 minutes for free in a public repository, saves MINT's memory back into the repository and publishes a view-only dashboard on GitHub Pages. Keys stay in GitHub Secrets (checked: no key ends up in any uploaded file). Because the repository is public, no subscriber list is stored: everything is posted to the Telegram channel.

log.title: First cloud run worked
log.detail: All agents ran on GitHub with 0 errors: SEC feeds, Fed and jobs calendars, CoinGecko prices, Trump's Truth archive, Binance's Telegram channel and Groq all worked from the cloud. 8 messages were posted to the Telegram channel and MINT saved its memory back to GitHub.

log.title: Problem: Bitcoin's bad week was missed
log.detail: The first cloud run kept 0 Bitcoin stories while Bitcoin fell and ETFs saw over $1bn of outflows: every story came from websites not on my approved list. I added well-known specialist outlets (CoinDesk, The Block, Decrypt for crypto; Kitco for gold; MarketWatch and Barron's). Also: 'China extends gold-buying streak' was wrongly dropped (added keywords to G4), and website sections like 'Investment' were treated as news (now ignored).

log.title: Problem: still 0 Bitcoin stories, and one story counted 4 times
log.detail: The second cloud run again kept 0 Bitcoin stories even with CoinDesk, The Block and Decrypt approved: Google News only shows the ~100 most popular stories and none came from my approved sites. Fix: the Scouts now ALSO search inside the approved news websites only (site: search). Second problem: the World Gold Council's Q3 report became 4 separate events (WSJ story, two WGC pages, the 'Gold Market Primer'), so one story counted as 4 'right' predictions and made accuracy look better than it was. Fix: stories with the same factor on the same day that share key words are now one event, website sections are removed, and old memory is cleaned up automatically. Supervisor tests: 22 of 22.

log.title: Decision: search ONLY the approved websites; more social accounts
log.detail: Instead of searching all of Google News and then rejecting stories from unapproved websites, the Scouts now search only inside the approved websites (site: search), so approved stories can never be crowded out by small websites. Social Watcher: added the Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank (official Bluesky accounts) and Watcher.Guru (Telegram), and switched Whale Alert on (only hack-type posts count). Elon Musk could not be added: he posts only on X, which has no free way to read posts. The cloud schedule was moved to minutes 7, 22, 37 and 52, because GitHub often delays or skips runs planned for :00.

log.title: Decision: run every 5 minutes
log.detail: GitHub Actions is free for public repositories, and its fastest schedule is every 5 minutes, so MINT now runs at :02, :07, :12 and so on. GitHub does not promise exact times: busy periods can delay or skip runs. Other free limits checked: Groq is only used once per new event, CoinGecko allows far more requests than MINT makes, and the cloud keeps only the newest 10 result files of each kind so the repository stays small. Risk: Google News may refuse some searches if MINT searches too often; MINT then shows an error for that search and carries on.

log.title: Fix: crypto post filed under gold
log.detail: First run with approved-only search: 9 Bitcoin stories found (before: 0), and the old duplicate events were cleaned up as planned. Problem: a Whale Alert post 'Crypto market weakens as traders watch ... for Fed clues' was filed as a GOLD event because it mentioned the Fed. Fix: a post about crypto is never filed under gold just for mentioning the Fed. Posts are also tidied (emojis at the start and 'Read Analysis' at the end removed).

log.title: Telegram messages readable at a glance
log.detail: Every Telegram message now starts with two short lines: what it is (🚨 alert, 👀 watch, ℹ️ info, ⌛ not confirmed, 📅 heads-up, ✅/❌ result) and how much it matters (🔴 high / 🟠 medium / 🟡 low impact, 📈 up / 📉 down, confidence bars ▰▰▰). The channel gets a one-time 'How to read MINT messages' key to pin. Telegram tests: 20 of 20.

log.title: History page improved
log.detail: Problems seen in History: an event showed a prediction (Bitcoin down) but its result said 'No prediction' (the Decision agent adds predictions AFTER the Price Tracker judges); old social posts still had emojis and 'Read Analysis'; a crypto post was still listed under gold; nothing showed between the 1-hour and 1-day prices; the legend said 0.1% while results use 1.5%/0.5%; and one old story made the average delay 51 hours. Fixes: results are judged again after the Decision agent; old posts are tidied and re-checked; new 'So far' column (move from the first report until now); 'result in X h' countdown; impact (High/Medium/Low) and confidence bars like in Telegram; accuracy per asset; typical delay uses the median; on the public website the past events library is view-only.

log.title: 'Run complete' message
log.detail: When a run finds nothing new, MINT now posts a short note to the Telegram channel ('MINT run complete - nothing new to report', with Bitcoin and Gold status), so I can see it is running. It is sent silently (no notification sound), because at every 5 minutes that could be up to 288 notes a day. Telegram tests: 21 of 21.

log.title: Decision: one reliable source is enough
log.detail: I removed the 'second source' rule. The approved list (sources.json) only contains reliable organisations, so if one of them reports an event it is confirmed straight away and goes to the Decision agent. Waiting for a second source only delayed alerts (e.g. the WSJ's Binance hack story waited for hours). Watch now means only one thing: a social media post, which MINT tracks for its impact but which still needs an approved news or official source before an alert, because accounts can be hacked (the SEC's X account in January 2024). Supervisor tests updated: 22 of 22.

log.title: Better way to judge predictions: 9 price checks
log.detail: The History page said '33% accuracy' without explaining how success was measured, and one 1-day price decided everything. Now MINT checks the price 9 times after the first report (1 h, 5 h, 10 h, 1 day, 36 h, 2 days, 3.5 days, 5 days, 7 days). A check only counts if the move is bigger than normal wiggle, and the bar grows with time (Bitcoin 0.3% after 1 h up to 4% after 7 days; gold 0.1% up to 1.3%), because prices wiggle more the longer you wait. An event is Right if more clear checks went the predicted way than the other way; the first result comes after 1 day and it is final after 7 days. The History page explains this, shows 'Price checks right' and 'Events judged right' separately, and a new table shows accuracy by time after the event. Telegram sends a result after 1 day and a final result after 7 days with every check (✅/❌/➖), and social media events now say '📱 From social media: <account>'. Tests: Supervisor 24/24, Telegram 21/21.

log.title: Impact size and duration; approved social accounts count alone
log.detail: Right/wrong alone hid useful information: e.g. 'WGC lowers outlook' was judged Wrong, but gold DID fall 0.5% for about 7 hours before rising. MINT now measures every event's impact from the hourly prices: how far the price moved the predicted way, when it peaked, and how long the effect lasted before it faded (shown as 📏 on the website and in Telegram results). Also: posts from approved social media accounts (social_accounts.json) now count as an approved source on their own, like approved news websites - every message says '📱 From social media: <account>' so the reader knows. Tests: Supervisor 24/24, Telegram 21/21.
